title: 31 Automated text message examples that sound like you
summary: Use these automated text message examples for reminders, follow-ups, requests and more. Make texting simple without losing a personal touch.
body_markdown:
If you’ve ever set *yourself* a reminder to send reminders or follow-up texts to your customers, this article is for you.


Manually texting customers one at a time doesn’t scale. Plus, it costs your business money through lost customers and forgotten follow-ups.


But automating repetitive text messages doesn’t mean your company will start sounding like a bot. All you need is the right templates to get you started. That is: templates that sound like *you* , keep you compliant, and reach your customers at the right time.


In this article, we’ll show you how to get started with automated text message examples you can steal — without sounding like a robot.


##


31 Examples of automated text messages by use case


One quick way to start automating is to gather a series of text message templates for your most common, repetitive[customer text messages](https://www.quo.com/blog/sample-text-messages-to-customers/) . Here are some examples to get you started:


A note on SMS compliance before you start
The TCPA, or[Telephone Consumer Protection Act](https://www.quo.com/blog/tcpa-compliance-checklist/) , governs business text messaging. One TCPA requirement is that businesses need written opt-in before sending any promotional or marketing texts. A few basics to follow for automated texts:
Identify yourself clearly in the first initial text.Include a clear opt-out message, like “Reply STOP to unsubscribe,” in every automated message.Only send texts between 8 a.m. and 9 p.m. in the recipient’s time zone.
Read our full guide to[SMS compliance](https://www.quo.com/blog/sms-compliance/) for more information.


###


**Appointment confirmation** **text templates**


A confirmation text helps[reduce no-shows](https://www.quo.com/blog/reduce-no-shows/) and confusion. The customer sees the date and time in writing when the booking is still top of mind. Be sure to state your business name. This is for compliance and helps customers quickly understand what the confirmation is for. Use one of these templates:


**To confirm an appointment request:**


Hi \[customer name\], \[business name\] has received your request for an upcoming appointment at our office. Please remember to fill out all new patient information before your visit on \[date, time\]. Please respond with YES to confirm your appointment. To opt out of text messages, reply STOP.


**Standard appointment confirmation text:**


Hi \[customer name\], your service appointment with \[business name\] for \[service type\] on \[date\] at \[time\] is confirmed. The estimated service time is \[duration\]. Reply CONFIRM to lock in this time or CHANGE to reschedule. Reply STOP to opt out of messages.


**To confirm a cancellation:**


Hi \[customer name\], we’ve canceled your appointment as you requested. If you’d like to reschedule, please respond with a date and time. Text STOP to opt out of future messages.


Tired of sending these manually? You can automate them. For example, you can connect a business phone system like Quo with[Zapier](https://www.quo.com/integrations/zapier) . This lets you automatically send a confirmation when someone books through Calendly. That way, you put customers’ minds at ease without doing the manual work.


💡 **Further reading:** Get 30+ more[appointment confirmation text templates](https://www.quo.com/blog/appointment-confirmation-text/) based on industry, use case, and more.


###


**Appointment reminder** **text examples**


Reminder texts are a great next step. They’re another repetitive, ongoing text that’s tricky to manage manually, easy to automate, and can reduce no-shows when you send them consistently. We recommend sending at least two reminder texts — one about a week out and one 24–48 hours before the appointment.


**Advance notice template:**


Hi \[customer name\], this is \[name\] from \[business name\]. Just a friendly reminder about your appointment on \[date\] at \[time\]. We look forward to seeing you! Reply STOP to opt out of future messages.


**24-hour template:**


\[Business name\]: Reminder \[customer name\], you have an appointment tomorrow at \[time\]. Reply YES to confirm or call \[number\] to reschedule. Text STOP to opt out of future messages.


**Reminder with a request for documents:**


Hi \[customer name\], I’m \[name\] from \[business name\]. I’m reaching out to confirm your appointment for \[day, date, time\] and let you know that we’ll need the following documents to \[action item\]: 1. \[Document 1\] 2. \[Document 2\]. Text STOP to opt out of future messages.


Ready to automate these as well? You can do it with Quo + Zapier. Here’s an automation you can copy.


**💡More ideas:** Get 25+ more[appointment reminder text templates](https://www.quo.com/blog/appointment-reminder-text/) based on use case and industry.


###


**Payment and invoice reminders**


Few things are worse than having to continually follow up with a customer to make sure the invoice gets paid. But it often must be done.


Pre-written text reminders make it easier. Here are three templates to get you started:


**For an upcoming payment due:**


Hi \[client name\], it’s \[company name\]. Just a gentle reminder that invoice \[#\] is due on \[date\]. Pay anytime by logging into your payment portal here: \[URL\]. Please note that a late payment fee of \[$X or X%\] will apply to any payment made after \[date\]. Let us know if you have any questions. Reply STOP to opt out of text reminders.


**For a past-due payment:**


Hi \[client name\], this is \[your name\] from \[company name\]. Your payment of \[$ amount\] for invoice \[#\] is \[X days\] overdue. You can pay by credit card, ACH, or eCheck here: \[URL\]. Reply STOP to opt out of text reminders.


**If you’re offering a payment plan:**


Hi \[client name\], it’s \[company name\]. Your invoice \[#\] is due on \[date\]. You can review and pay here: \[payment link\]. If you’d like to set up a payment plan, you can pay in \[#\] installments. Set up a payment plan here: \[URL\]. Reply STOP to opt out of future texts.


**💡More inspiration:** Get 15+ more examples of text and email templates for[payment reminders](https://www.quo.com/blog/payment-reminder-message/) .


###


**After-hours auto-reply text message examples**


After-hours automated responses significantly increase[speed to lead](https://www.quo.com/blog/speed-to-lead/) . Customers get replies faster, which can have a huge impact. Data from[Drift](https://www.salesloft.com/resources/guides/conversational-ai-marketing-trends-report) shows reps who sent a first response within two minutes had the highest chance of booking a meeting.


Wait a day or two, and the customer has likely moved on to a competitor. Here are some auto-reply templates to use:


**Standard after-hours template:**


Hi there! Thanks for contacting \[business name\]. We’re away from our desks at the moment. Our standard office hours are \[hours, days\]. We’ll give you a call back as soon as we’re back in the office. If you’re getting in touch about an appointment, you can book online at \[URL\]. Text STOP to opt out of future SMS messages.


Note: If you’re a service or healthcare business with an after-hours or emergency number, it’s a good idea to include that number in this text as well.


**Holiday or** **out-of-office message** **template:**


Hey, thanks for contacting \[business name\]. Our office is currently closed for \[reason\]. Our standard office hours are \[hours\]. We’ll give you a call back as soon as we’re back in the office. Reply STOP to opt out of future texts.


**Message receipt confirmation template:**


Thanks for messaging \[business name\]. We received your message and are looking forward to helping you! We’ll review and respond as soon as we’re back in the office. Our standard office hours are \[days, hours\]. Reply STOP to opt out of future texts.


**After-hours with next steps:**


Hello! Thanks for contacting \[business name\]. We received your message and will review and respond as soon as we’re back in the office. In the meantime, please \[action items\] so we can take care of you as quickly as possible. To opt out of texts in the future, reply STOP.


Action items can include self-service options like:


- Creating an account on your website
- Filling out a new patient or new client form
- Completing documents or intake paperwork and uploading them to an online portal


With Quo, automated text responses are simple. You can set up[auto-reply templates](https://www.quo.com/blog/texting-auto-reply-examples/) for missed texts, voicemails, and calls — both during and after hours. That way, every customer gets a quick response every time.


💡 **More ideas:** If none of these work, check out more[after-hours text templates](https://www.quo.com/blog/after-business-hours-text-message/) to get started with.


###


**Follow-up messages**


Follow-up messages are some of the easiest to forget but some of the most important to remember. Try one or more of these templates to make follow-ups easier and more consistent:


**Following up on a quote/estimate:**


Hi \[client\], just circling back on the quote I sent from \[business name\]. Can you let me know where things stand? I’ll hold off on next steps till I hear from you! Thanks, \[name\]. Text STOP to opt out of future messages.


**No response after the first text:**


Hi \[client\]. I’m \[name\] from \[company name\]. I wanted to follow up on my previous message about \[topic\] and schedule a quick call to understand your needs. Would any time between \[time range, date\] work for you? Text STOP to opt out of future messages.


**Following up after a demo:**


Hi \[client\], hope the \[business name\] demo was helpful! If anything comes up, feel free to text me here. Happy to help however I can. Text STOP to opt out of future messages.


**Following up on an upsell offer:**


Hi \[client\], just checking in! Are you still considering the \[business name\] \[add-on product/service\]? If you’d like to move forward, I can get it set up this week. Text STOP to opt out of future messages.


Key piece to keep in mind: **keep it simple.** No need to overthink the follow-up. The goal is to stay top of mind and be available when your client is ready to move forward.


And yes — follow-up texts can be automated too.

###


**Welcome and opt-in messages**


Starting on the right foot can make the difference between warm leads going cold or becoming loyal customers. Try implementing one of these welcome or[opt-in text messages](https://www.quo.com/blog/what-does-opt-mean-in-text/) :


**Confirming opt-in consent:**


Hey \[name\], this is \[name\] from \[business\]. You filled out an online form and gave us this number. Are you okay with receiving updates and reminders at this number? Text YES to confirm or STOP to opt out.


**Introducing a point of contact:**


Hi \[customer name\], I’m \[your name\]. I’m part of the \[business name\] team, and I’ll be your point of contact moving forward. Looking forward to working with you! Let me know if you need anything. Text STOP to opt out of future messages.


**Sharing getting-started resources:**


Hi \[customer name\], this is \[your name\] from \[business name\]. Thanks for choosing us! Just wanted to share \[resource\], which can help you get started: \[URL\]. If you have any questions or need help getting set up, feel free to text me here. Text STOP to opt out of future text messages.


**💡Need more ideas for welcome messages?** We’ve got you covered with[introduction text examples](https://www.quo.com/blog/introduction-text/) and[welcome text templates](https://www.quo.com/blog/welcome-text-message/) you can use.


###


**Feedback request automated text example**


One of the easiest ways to collect more customer feedback and improve customer satisfaction is to automate feedback requests. Many customers *do* mean to give great feedback, but they need reminders. And remembering to ask directly can fall to the end of your to-do list or even feel awkward. Here’s how to ask for feedback quickly and easily:


**If you want direct feedback:**


Hi \[client name\], it’s \[name\] from \[business name\]. How’d everything go with your \[service\] today? Reply and let me know on a scale of one to five, with five being great! Good or bad, I read every one. Reply STOP to opt out.


**If you want feedback through a link:**


Hi \[client\], your input means a lot to us. It helps us improve and serve you better. Mind sharing your thoughts on \[product/service\] here? \[Link\] Text STOP to opt out of future messages.


###


**Reengagement automated text templates**


Have a client or lead go cold? A great text can bring them back. Making this part of your routine can help you get more value from existing or previous clients. Try one of these win-back templates:


**Share a limited-time offer:**


Hi \[client\], it’s \[name\] from \[company name\]. It’s been a while! Just wanted to share: our \[offer\] wraps up Friday. Want in? Reply YES, and we’ll get you set up. Reply STOP to opt out.


**Seasonal check-in:**


Hi \[client name\], it’s \[name\] from \[business name\]. \[Season/time of year\] is when \[service\] tends to matter most. Want to get on the calendar before it gets busy? Reply YES, and I’ll set you up. Reply STOP to opt out.


**Recurring-service nudge:**


Hi \[client name\], it’s been \[timeframe\] since your last \[service\] with \[business name\]. Ready to get back on the schedule? Reply YES, and I’ll get you booked. Reply STOP to opt out.


###


**Automated text message** **templates for promotion and loyalty offers**


Text messages can be a great way to increase sales and engagement on promotions and offers. According to data from Klaviyo,[86% o consumers](https://www.klaviyo.com/blog/sms-stats) surveyed made two or more purchases in the last year from SMS messages. Try one of these templates:


**General promotion text:**


\[Business name\]: Our \[offer\] ends Friday, \[name\]. Call \[business number\] or book now at \[URL\] before spots fill up. Reply STOP to opt out.


**For a loyalty promotion or early access:**


Thanks for being a loyal \[company name\] customer. To show our thanks, we’re treating you to \[offer\]. Get early access now: \[link\]. Text STOP to opt out of future text messages.


**For milestone or anniversary offers:**


Hi \[client name\]! Congrats on the \[#\] anniversary of \[event\]. To celebrate, we’re giving you \[offer\] at \[business name\]. Claim yours here: \[link\]. Text STOP to opt out of future text messages.


###


**Order, delivery, and pickup updates**


A customer who just placed an order or booked a pickup wants to know it went through. Otherwise, they might put in the order again or contact you for updates. Here are some templates you can use to put people’s minds at ease:


**Order ready for pickup text template:**


Hi \[client name\], your \[company name\] order is ready for pickup at \[location\]. Please pick up your order by \[date\]. Our store hours are \[days, hours\]. Reply STOP to opt out of future texts.


**Item shipped text:**


Good news, \[customer name\], your items from \[company name\] have shipped! We can’t wait for you to receive them. You can check your order status here: \[tracking URL\]. Reply STOP to opt out of future texts.


**Abandoned cart text template:**


Hey there, we noticed you still have a few items in your \[company name\] cart. Ready to check out? We’ve got them saved for you here: \[link\]. Reply STOP to opt out of future texts.

6 Ways to set up automated text messages


Once you have your templates ready, there are several ways to easily send text message automations. We’ll show you[how to set up automated text messages](https://www.quo.com/blog/how-to-send-automated-texts/) in Quo.


###


**1. Automate with Quo’s built-in auto-replies**


Quo lets you set up auto-replies in under a minute. The feature is built in, so you can copy-paste the automated text message examples through your settings.


On the web or desktop app, follow these four steps:


1. Log in to Quo and select **Settings.**
2. Select **Workspace.**
3. Click **Phone Numbers.** Choose the number you want to add auto-replies for.
4. Go to **Automations** , then scroll to **Auto-Replies.** Set up custom auto-replies based on any of these triggers during or after business hours:


- Incoming message
- Missed call without a voicemail
- Missed call with a voicemail


###


**2. Use scheduled messages**


Scheduled messages are perfect when you have a lower volume of messages to send, but you don’t want to remember to send each one yourself.


Here’s how to schedule texts in Quo:


1. Go to Quo’s web or desktop app.
2. Find the conversation you want to schedule a text for. Type or copy-paste the message.
3. Personalize messages, then click or tap the **Clock** icon.
4. Set whether to send the message if the recipient contacts you first or automatically unschedule it if they do.
5. Set the time to send your message.


**💡Pro tip:** Save the text message templates you use often in Quo as[snippets](https://support.quo.com/core-concepts/messaging/snippets) . That way, you can easily schedule them using your drop-down snippets list.


###

Thinking of writing the same follow-up to five different customers one at a time? Connect Quo to an AI model, like ChatGPT or[Claude](https://www.quo.com/blog/claude-integration/) , to save time. These can pull each conversation’s context and send a personalized follow-up to everyone who needs one, in a single pass.


Here’s how to set up Quo + Claude:


1. Open Claude, then go to **Customize** from the left sidebar.
2. Click **Connectors,** then search for and select **Quo.**
3. Click **Connect** , then click **Allow** on the next screen.


From there, you can ask Claude to search your Quo data and message history and send texts for you. ###


**4. Set up** **automated text messages** **using Zapier**


You can use Zapier to combine Quo with other platforms or tools you use. This way, you can automate appointment reminders, confirmations, and other scheduling-based texts based on information created and stored in other platforms.


Here’s a[Zapier example](https://www.quo.com/blog/zapier-examples/) combining Quo + Acuity Scheduling:


1. Open **Zapier** and click **+** **Create** . ****
2. Select **Zap workflows** .
3. Select **Acuity Scheduling** as the Trigger App and **New Appointment** as the Trigger Event.
4. Add an Action and select **Quo** . Choose **Send a message** as the Action Event. Then customize the message that’ll be sent.


Whenever someone books through Acuity Scheduling, they’ll automatically receive a confirmation text.


If you’re setting up appointment reminders or need some time to pass between an appointment being scheduled and the text going out, add a Delay step. Here’s how:


1. Click on the **+** sign between the Acuity and Quo steps.
2. Choose **Delay** . ****
3. Select **Delay For** and add the delay time you want.

###


**5. Set up** **automated text messages** **using Make**


Not a Zapier user? You can also set up automated texts using[Make](https://www.quo.com/integrations/make) . Let’s say you want to send out welcome texts when your customers fill out a web form.


Here’s how to set it up:


1. Log in to Make and create a new scenario.
2. Select **Typeform** as the first module. Choose **Watch Responses** as the trigger.
3. Add a **Phone Number** module and select **Parse a phone number** to format submitted numbers.
4. Add a **Quo** module and select **Create a contact** . This will save the submitted details to your Quo contacts.
5. Add another **Quo** module and select **Send a text message (SMS).** Then set up the automated text message you want to send.


###


**6. Automate texts based on more custom triggers using the API**


For even more customized workflows, use the[Quo API](https://www.quo.com/docs/mdx/api-reference/send-your-first-message) to send text messages. This is a developer tool that lets you trigger a text based on something specific to your setup. You don’t have to rely on Zapier or Make’s list of pre-built triggers. For example, you could:


- Send customer notifications like order updates based on website data
- Send marketing automations like promotional campaigns
- Send automated feedback requests a certain number of days after a purchase was made


To use it, go to **Settings** , then **API** in your Quo workspace. Then, generate an API key. You can use this key to make custom triggers for automated text messages from other events across your tech stack.


FYI: Messages sent this way are billed at $0.01 per segment from your prepaid Voice & Messaging Balance.

##


7 Best practices for automating text messages


Getting started with automating text messages can feel overwhelming. You don’t want to annoy customers, sound too robotic, or break any rules. Follow these best practices to make sure your automated text messages land well with your customers:


1. **Stay compliant.** Make sure you get written consent to send text messages to each contact. Identify your business and include an opt-out option on every automated text.
2. **Keep message frequency manageable.** For promotional messages, stick with two to four per month or less. You don’t want to overwhelm or spam customers.
3. **Personalize when possible.**[Customers are 3.7x more likely](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-06-04-marketing-leaders-can-unlock-commercial-value-by-redefining-personalized-digital-interactions-with-customer-shared-data) to “purchase more than intended when they feel their experience is personalized.”
4. **Keep it short.** No one wants to read a wall of text on their phone. Keep text messages around or[under 160 characters](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/47/64.1200#:~:text=(D)%20The%20voice%20call%20or%20text%20message%20notification%20must%20be%20concise%2C%20generally%20one%20minute%20or%20less%20in%20length%20for%20voice%20calls%20or%20160%20characters%20or%20less%20in%20length%20for%20text%20messages%3B) .
5. **Test workflows internally.** Make sure automations are working as expected using your own phone number first. That way, you avoid having to automate a mass “Whoops!” text.
6. **Acknowledge the automation.** A simple “This is an automated reminder from \[company name\]” helps set the right expectation for the customer. It can also help them feel less deterred by automated texts.
7. **Know when** ***not*** **to automate.** If a workflow typically ends with customers requesting to speak to a human, un-automate it. Not every workflow is a good fit for automation. Save your energy for places where customers expect and need real-time[conversational messaging](https://www.openphone.com/blog/conversational-messaging/) .

FAQs


**How do automated text messages work?**


Automated text messages are texts sent out automatically based on a predetermined trigger. They can run on a schedule, like a reminder sent 24 hours before an appointment. They can be triggered by a customer action, like a text after booking an appointment.
You don’t need to know how to code to automate text messages. Quo can help you using built-in tools like auto-replies or third-party integrations with apps like Zapier.


**Why are automated text messages important for businesses?**


Automated text messages make sure your customers get the reminders, follow-ups, and information they need when they need it. You never forget to follow up, but you don’t have to be on call 24/7. This can improve customer engagement and satisfaction and increase sales and conversions.


**Is automated texting TCPA compliant?**


Automating a text doesn’t change what’s legally required to send it. You still need consent before texting someone and a clear opt-out in every message. You also have to stay compliant with TCPA requirements and any other applicable regulations. When in doubt, consult with a legal professional about state and federal requirements.


**What are the different types of automated messages?**


Common types of automated messages include:
– **Transactional messages** , e.g., messages that confirm a transaction, booked appointment, or registration
– **Time-based reminders** , e.g., follow-ups and appointment reminders
– **Autoresponders** , e.g., automatic responses to customer calls or texts after hours
– **Promotional messages** , e.g., promoting a new sale, service, or offer to an existing audience
– **Reengagement messages,** e.g., abandoned cart, special offers, or upsell messages based on timing or customer behavior


**How long should auto-reply messages be?**


Auto-reply messages should be short and to the point — no longer than needed to get your message across. A good rule of thumb is to stay under 160 characters.
